public_rationale: He asks a question and answers with an opinion: "I don't think so!" He backs it with a study that "suggested" a slowdown. That study is real: METR's July 2025 trial found experienced open-source developers took 19% longer with early-2025 AI tools, which METR called a snapshot of one setting. But he names no group of users, no tools, no period, and no measure of speed. Scoring the sentence would mean treating a hedged opinion as a firm claim and inventing its scope, which earlier reviews found unfair to him. So I treat it as an opinion that cannot be checked. His description of the cited study is accurate.
limitations: A firmer version, such as 'AI tools slow experienced developers on their own codebases,' could be tested, but he did not state it.
